intro: At B2 you linked ideas with **although**, **despite**, **whereas** and **Nevertheless,**. At C1 your texts get longer, and they need to hang together. You'll add formal connectors (**albeit**, **notwithstanding**, **insofar as**, **hence**, **whereby**, **in that**), point back clearly with **the former / the latter** and **this approach**, and guide your reader through a long report with signposts like **Turning now to …** and **As outlined above, …**.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line from b2-linking-words (don't re-teach it): although / whereas + subject + verb, despite / in spite of + noun or -ing, Nevertheless, / Consequently, / Moreover, at the start of a new sentence with a comma, and one linker per sentence. New here: cohesion (kohesi) = a text that hangs together: the reader always knows what 'this', 'it' or 'the latter' points to, and where the argument is going. Three tools, one per objective: formal connectors, reference devices, signposting. Explain jargon the first time in plain Indonesian: cohesion (teks yang menyambung), connector (kata penghubung), reference (rujukan: kata yang merujuk balik), summary noun (kata benda yang merangkum ide sebelumnya), signposting (penunjuk arah dalam teks), clause (subjek + kata kerja), noun phrase (kata benda dengan kata-kata kecilnya). Everything here is formal written English (reports, essays, theses, official letters); in chat and meetings but / so / also / anyway stay natural. Say honestly that many choices here are style, and only test grammar errors and clear meaning.

Formal connectors and their grammar (objective formal-connectors). albeit (meskipun) + an adjective, adverb or noun phrase, mid-sentence after a comma: effective, albeit expensive; progress, albeit slowly; a success, albeit a small one. NOT albeit + a full clause and not at the start of a sentence: the node's common error *'The plan was effective, albeit it was expensive' → albeit expensive (or although it was expensive). notwithstanding (meskipun ada / terlepas dari) = despite + noun, very formal (reports, contracts, law); it can also follow the noun (the costs notwithstanding). Common error *'Notwithstanding of the costs' (mixing it with in spite of). 'notwithstanding the fact that + clause' is a phrase to remember: accept it, don't test it. insofar as (sejauh / sepanjang) + subject + verb = to the extent that; British also writes 'in so far as': accept both. in that (dalam arti bahwa) + subject + verb = because, explaining in what way the first part is true (risky in that it depends on one supplier); don't confuse it with 'in which'.

hence / thus (oleh karena itu) = therefore, very formal. Thus, starts a new sentence like Therefore,. hence is most often followed by a noun phrase with no verb: '…; hence the delay' (= that is why there was a delay); 'Hence,' at the start of a sentence is also correct. Accept '…, thus reducing costs' if the learner writes it, but don't teach it (a result participle clause). whereby (dengan mana / yang dengannya) comes after a noun such as system, scheme, agreement, process, arrangement = by which / under which: a scheme whereby staff can work from home; 'where' is common in less formal writing. The Indonesian trap and the node's common error: 'Meskipun …, tetapi …' / 'Karena …, maka …' → *'Although the plan is risky, but it is worth trying': English uses ONE linker (Although …, it … / … , but …).

Reference devices (objective reference-devices). the former (yang pertama / yang disebut duluan) / the latter (yang kedua / yang disebut terakhir): only for exactly TWO things; with three or more, use the first / the last or repeat the name. They also go before a noun (the latter option). this / these + a summary noun instead of a bare this: this approach, this trend, this decision, these findings. such a + singular countable / such + plural or uncountable (seperti itu): such a view, such measures, such information; *'such a measures' is wrong. A vague this or it that could point to two things must be fixed with a noun or a name: 'The ministry cut the budget and raised fees. This angered students.' → This fee rise …; 'Pak Hasan told Budi that he would lead the project' → name the person. Indonesian trap: hal ini / hal tersebut becomes *'this matter' / *'the said matter' in every sentence; 'program tersebut' → this / the programme, not *'the mentioned programme'.

Signposting (objective signposting): the map of a long text. Next topic: Turning now to + noun, … (a fixed phrase to remember, so it doesn't need a matching subject) / Having considered X, we now turn to Y (participle clause from b2-participle-clauses: the subject after it must be the one who considered: *'Having considered the benefits, the risks will now be discussed' ✗). Pointing back: As outlined above, … / As mentioned earlier, … / As discussed in Section 2, …. Pointing forward: As will be discussed below, … / This will be explained in Section 4. Back to the thread or closing: To return to the main point, … / In summary, …. In writing: above (earlier) and below (later); in a talk: as I mentioned earlier / as we'll see later. Signposts belong at the start of a paragraph or section, not in every sentence. Indonesian 'seperti yang telah disebutkan di atas' → as mentioned above, not *'as above mentioned'.

Grammar limits: A0–B2 grammar (incl. participle clauses, non-defining relative clauses, all passives) plus this lesson. Keep other C1 structures out: no inversion (Not only …, Never before …), no cleft sentences (What matters is …, It is X that …), no subjunctive, no impersonal passives (It is argued that …), no nominalisation as a topic. Don't teach the aforementioned, hereinafter, the said or henceforth: if the learner uses them, accept them and say they sound legal or old-fashioned. Contexts: ministries, universities, startups, NGOs, city councils, reports and theses (Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, Yogyakarta, rupiah). When the learner writes a paragraph, praise the logic first, then correct ONE thing: usually albeit + clause, 'notwithstanding of', two linkers in one sentence, the former/latter with three items, or a vague this.

keyPoints.title: Formal connectors: the grammar still decides
keyPoints.explanation: albeit + an adjective, adverb or noun phrase (effective, albeit expensive), never + a full clause. notwithstanding + a noun, like despite (Notwithstanding the costs, … / the costs notwithstanding), never 'notwithstanding of'. insofar as + subject + verb = to the extent that. in that + subject + verb = because, saying in what way something is true. hence (+ a noun) / Thus, = therefore, very formal. whereby after a noun = by which. And only one linker per sentence: not 'Although …, but …'.

examples.en: The new system is effective, albeit expensive.
Notwithstanding the costs, the ministry approved the project.
examples.id: Meskipun biayanya besar, kementerian menyetujui proyek itu.

examples.en: The plan worked insofar as traffic fell in the city centre.
examples.id: Rencananya berhasil sejauh lalu lintas di pusat kota berkurang.

id.title: Kata penghubung formal: tata bahasa tetap yang menentukan
id.explanation: albeit + kata sifat, kata keterangan atau frasa kata benda (effective, albeit expensive), tidak pernah + klausa lengkap. notwithstanding + kata benda, seperti despite (Notwithstanding the costs, … / the costs notwithstanding), tidak pernah 'notwithstanding of'. insofar as + subjek + kata kerja = sejauh / sepanjang. in that + subjek + kata kerja = karena, menjelaskan dalam hal apa sesuatu benar. hence (+ kata benda) / Thus, = oleh karena itu, sangat formal. whereby setelah kata benda = yang dengannya. Dan hanya satu kata penghubung per kalimat: bukan 'Although …, but …'.

keyPoints.title: Point back clearly
keyPoints.explanation: With exactly two things, the former = the first one and the latter = the second one; with three or more, say the first / the last or use the name. Instead of a bare this, add a summary noun: this approach, this trend, these findings. such a + one thing (such a view), such + plural (such measures). If this or it could point to two things, name the thing or the person.

examples.en: Staff can travel by MRT or by car. The former is faster in the rush hour.
examples.id: Staf bisa naik MRT atau mobil. Yang pertama (MRT) lebih cepat saat jam sibuk.

examples.en: Online shopping keeps growing. This trend has hit small shops hard.
examples.id: Belanja online terus tumbuh. Tren ini sangat memukul toko-toko kecil.

examples.en: Some argue that AI will replace translators. Such a view ignores the need for human judgement.
examples.id: Ada yang berpendapat AI akan menggantikan penerjemah. Pandangan seperti itu mengabaikan perlunya penilaian manusia.

id.title: Merujuk balik dengan jelas
id.explanation: Kalau ada tepat dua hal, the former = yang pertama dan the latter = yang kedua; kalau tiga atau lebih, pakai the first / the last atau sebut namanya. Daripada this saja, tambahkan kata benda yang merangkum: this approach, this trend, these findings. such a + satu hal (such a view), such + jamak (such measures). Kalau this atau it bisa merujuk ke dua hal, sebut nama benda atau orangnya.

keyPoints.title: Signpost a long text
keyPoints.explanation: Signposts tell the reader where they are. Next topic: Turning now to …, / Having considered X, we now turn to Y. Back: As outlined above, … / As mentioned earlier, … Forward: As will be discussed below, … Back to the thread or the end: To return to the main point, … / In summary, … In writing, above = earlier and below = later. Put signposts at the start of a paragraph or section.

examples.en: Turning now to the costs, the figures are more mixed.
examples.id: Beralih sekarang ke biayanya, angkanya lebih beragam.

examples.en: Having considered the benefits, we now turn to the risks.
examples.id: Setelah membahas manfaatnya, sekarang kita beralih ke risikonya.

examples.en: As will be discussed below, some clients were unhappy.
examples.id: Seperti yang akan dibahas di bawah, beberapa klien tidak puas.

id.title: Beri penunjuk arah di teks panjang
id.explanation: Penunjuk arah (signpost) memberi tahu pembaca di mana mereka berada. Topik berikutnya: Turning now to …, / Having considered X, we now turn to Y. Merujuk ke belakang: As outlined above, … / As mentioned earlier, … Ke depan: As will be discussed below, … Kembali ke inti atau penutup: To return to the main point, … / In summary, … Dalam tulisan, above = sebelumnya dan below = nanti. Taruh penunjuk arah di awal paragraf atau bagian.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: Although the deadline is tight, but the team can still finish the report on time.
expected: although the deadline is tight the team can still finish the report on time
even though the deadline is tight the team can still finish the report on time
the deadline is tight but the team can still finish the report on time
the team can still finish the report on time although the deadline is tight
guidedPractice.hint: Meskipun …, tetapi … uses two linkers, but English uses one. Keep although and drop but, or keep but and drop although.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: The new MRT line has been effective, albeit it was expensive to build.
expected: the new mrt line has been effective albeit expensive to build
the new mrt line has been effective albeit expensive
the new mrt line has been effective although it was expensive to build
the new mrt line has been effective even though it was expensive to build
guidedPractice.hint: albeit takes a short phrase (an adjective like expensive), not a subject + verb (it was). Drop it was, or change albeit to although.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write one formal word: The two universities have an agreement ___ students can take courses at both campuses.
expected: whereby
guidedPractice.hint: After a noun like agreement, scheme or system, this word means 'by which / under which' and is followed by subject + verb.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rina compared two laptops: a cheap Lenovo and an expensive MacBook. She bought ___ because her budget was only Rp 8 million. Write the former or the latter.
expected: the former
guidedPractice.hint: The former = the first of the two things mentioned; the latter = the second. Which laptop fits a small budget, and which was mentioned first?

guidedPractice.prompt: Write the word that points to a LATER part of a written report: As will be discussed ___, the survey had some limitations.
expected: below
later
guidedPractice.hint: In writing, earlier parts are 'above' and later parts are ...

independentPractice.prompt: Join the two sentences with insofar as: The policy is successful. It has reduced traffic in the city centre.
expected: the policy is successful insofar as it has reduced traffic in the city centre
the policy is successful in so far as it has reduced traffic in the city centre
the policy has been successful insofar as it has reduced traffic in the city centre
independentPractice.hint: insofar as + subject + verb = to the extent that. It goes in the middle: The policy is successful insofar as it …

independentPractice.prompt: Make 'This' clear by adding a noun after it: The company cut its training budget by half. This upset many young staff.
expected: this decision upset many young staff
this cut upset many young staff
this move upset many young staff
this change upset many young staff
this budget cut upset many young staff
the company cut its training budget by half this decision upset many young staff
the company cut its training budget by half this cut upset many young staff
independentPractice.hint: Use this + a summary noun that names what happened: this decision, this cut, this move …

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence that moves from Section 2 of a report (the survey results) to Section 3 (the recommendations). Start with Having considered.
expected: having considered the survey results we now turn to the recommendations
having considered the results we now turn to the recommendations
having considered the survey results we will now turn to the recommendations
having considered the survey results we now move on to the recommendations
independentPractice.hint: Having considered + what came before, then we (the people who considered) + now turn to + what comes next.

assessment.prompt: Write albeit, notwithstanding or insofar as. From a report on a recycling project in Surabaya: The pilot scheme was a success, ___ a modest one: only 40 households took part.
assessment.rubric: Correct: albeit (= although, before a short noun phrase: a modest one). 'notwithstanding' = 0 (it means despite and needs a noun that works against the main idea, not a description of the success). 'insofar as' = 0 (it needs a subject + verb after it). 'although' or 'though' = 60 (understandable meaning, but not one of the choices and less formal).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Notwithstanding of the protests, the city council approved the new toll road.
acceptableAnswers: notwithstanding the protests the city council approved the new toll road
the protests notwithstanding the city council approved the new toll road
the city council approved the new toll road notwithstanding the protests
despite the protests the city council approved the new toll road
in spite of the protests the city council approved the new toll road
the city council approved the new toll road despite the protests
the city council approved the new toll road in spite of the protests
assessment.rubric: Correct: Notwithstanding the protests, the city council approved the new toll road (notwithstanding + noun, no 'of'), or The protests notwithstanding, …. 'Despite the protests' / 'In spite of the protests' = 100 (correct, slightly less formal). 'Despite of the protests' = 20 (the same 'of' error). Unchanged sentence = 0. Small changes elsewhere in the sentence (e.g. 'the council') don't lose marks.

assessment.prompt: Write the missing word. From a news article: The new law is unusual ___ that it lets workers choose two of their own public holidays.
assessment.rubric: Correct: in (in that + subject + verb = because, explaining in what way the law is unusual). 'in that' typed in full = 100. 'so' = 0 ('unusual so that' = in order that, wrong meaning). 'because' = 30 ('unusual because that it lets' is ungrammatical). 'for' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Write two words (not the name of a city). Dimas was offered two scholarships: one to study in Melbourne and one to study in Leiden. He accepted ___ because his partner already works in Leiden.
assessment.rubric: Correct: the latter (= the second of the two things mentioned: Leiden). 'the second' or 'the second one' = 60 (right meaning, but the lesson's reference word is the latter). 'latter' without 'the' = 60. 'the former' = 0 (that is Melbourne). 'the last' = 40 (used for three or more).

assessment.prompt: Write view, trend or approach. From a company report: Some managers believe that staff who work from home are lazy. However, such a ___ is not supported by the data from our survey.
assessment.rubric: Correct: view (such a view = an opinion like that; it sums up what the managers believe). 'belief' or 'claim' = 100 (also summary nouns for an opinion). 'trend' = 0 (a trend is a change over time, not an opinion). 'approach' = 20 (a way of doing something, not an opinion).

assessment.prompt: Write the missing word. A report on a four-day week trial moves from productivity to a new section: '___ now to staff opinions, most employees wanted the trial to continue.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: Turning (Turning now to + noun = moving to the next topic, a fixed signposting phrase). 'Moving' = 70 ('Moving on to staff opinions' is natural, but 'Moving now to' is less usual). 'Coming' = 60. 'Turn' = 40 (wrong form). 'According' = 0 (wrong meaning).

assessment.prompt: Write the missing word. The survey was described in Section 2 of a report, and Section 4 begins: 'As outlined ___, the survey covered 300 small businesses in Yogyakarta.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: above (in a written text, 'above' = earlier in the text). 'earlier' or 'previously' = 100. 'before' = 70 (understood, but less natural here). 'below' = 0 (that points forward, to a later part).

material.title: Cohesion: a text that hangs together

rows.en: Although the plan is risky, it is worth trying.
rows.id: Meskipun rencananya berisiko, rencana itu layak dicoba.

rows.en: The plan is risky, but it is worth trying.
The plan is risky. Nevertheless, it is worth trying.
rows.id: Rencananya berisiko. Namun demikian, rencana itu layak dicoba.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: **Meskipun …, tetapi …** and **Karena …, maka …** use two linkers. English uses **one**: `Although the plan is risky, but it is worth trying` ✗ → *Although the plan is risky, it is worth trying.* or *The plan is risky, but it is worth trying.* The new formal words follow the same rule: one connector for one link.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **Meskipun …, tetapi …** dan **Karena …, maka …** memakai dua kata penghubung. Bahasa Inggris memakai **satu**: `Although the plan is risky, but it is worth trying` ✗ → *Although the plan is risky, it is worth trying.* atau *The plan is risky, but it is worth trying.* Kata-kata formal yang baru juga ikut aturan yang sama: satu kata penghubung untuk satu hubungan.

options: Although sales fell, but the company kept all its staff.
Although sales fell, the company kept all its staff.
Despite sales fell, the company kept all its staff.
blocks.explain: One linker per sentence: **Although** + subject + verb (*sales fell*), then the main clause with no *but*. The first sentence has two linkers (*Meskipun …, tetapi …*). The third puts a subject + verb after *despite*, which needs a noun (*Despite falling sales, …*).

id.explain: Satu kata penghubung per kalimat: **Although** + subjek + kata kerja (*sales fell*), lalu klausa utama tanpa *but*. Kalimat pertama punya dua kata penghubung (*Meskipun …, tetapi …*). Kalimat ketiga menaruh subjek + kata kerja setelah *despite*, padahal despite butuh kata benda (*Despite falling sales, …*).

blocks.text:
At C1 the grammar still chooses the connector: look at **what comes after it**. A **clause** = subject + verb (*it was expensive*); a **phrase** = a few words with no subject + verb of their own (*expensive, slowly, a small one, the costs*).
- **albeit** (*meskipun*) = although, but only before a **short phrase**: an adjective (*albeit expensive*), an adverb (*albeit slowly*) or a noun phrase (*albeit a small one*). Never before a clause: `albeit it was expensive` ✗. It goes in the middle of the sentence, usually after a comma.
- **notwithstanding** (*meskipun ada / terlepas dari*) = despite + a noun: *Notwithstanding the costs, …* Very formal (reports, contracts, law). It can also come **after** the noun: *The costs notwithstanding, …* Never `notwithstanding of` ✗.
- **insofar as** (*sejauh / sepanjang*) + subject + verb = **to the extent that**: it limits how far something is true. British English also writes *in so far as*.
- **in that** (*dalam arti bahwa*) + subject + verb = because, explaining **in what way** the first part is true.
- **hence / thus** (*oleh karena itu*) = therefore, very formal. **Thus,** starts a new sentence like *Therefore,*. **hence** is often followed by just a noun, with no verb: *…; hence the delay* = that's why there was a delay.
- **whereby** (*yang dengannya*) comes after a noun like *system, scheme, agreement, process* = by which / under which, + subject + verb.

id.text:
Di C1 tata bahasa tetap yang memilih kata penghubungnya: lihat **apa yang datang setelahnya**. **Klausa** (clause) = subjek + kata kerja (*it was expensive*); **frasa** (phrase) = beberapa kata tanpa subjek + kata kerjanya sendiri (*expensive, slowly, a small one, the costs*).
- **albeit** (*meskipun*) = although, tapi hanya sebelum **frasa pendek**: kata sifat (*albeit expensive*), kata keterangan (*albeit slowly*) atau frasa kata benda (*albeit a small one*). Tidak pernah sebelum klausa: `albeit it was expensive` ✗. Posisinya di tengah kalimat, biasanya setelah koma.
- **notwithstanding** (*meskipun ada / terlepas dari*) = despite + kata benda: *Notwithstanding the costs, …* Sangat formal (laporan, kontrak, hukum). Bisa juga diletakkan **setelah** kata bendanya: *The costs notwithstanding, …* Tidak pernah `notwithstanding of` ✗.
- **insofar as** (*sejauh / sepanjang*) + subjek + kata kerja = **to the extent that**: membatasi sejauh mana sesuatu benar. Bahasa Inggris British juga menulis *in so far as*.
- **in that** (*dalam arti bahwa*) + subjek + kata kerja = karena, menjelaskan **dalam hal apa** bagian pertama itu benar.
- **hence / thus** (*oleh karena itu*) = therefore, sangat formal. **Thus,** memulai kalimat baru seperti *Therefore,*. **hence** sering diikuti kata benda saja, tanpa kata kerja: *…; hence the delay* = itulah sebabnya ada keterlambatan.
- **whereby** (*yang dengannya*) datang setelah kata benda seperti *system, scheme, agreement, process* = by which / under which, + subjek + kata kerja.

rows.en: The trial was a success, albeit a short one.
The bad weather notwithstanding, the festival went ahead.
rows.id: Terlepas dari cuaca buruk, festivalnya tetap berlangsung.

rows.en: The two cities are similar in that both grew around a port.
rows.id: Kedua kota itu mirip dalam arti keduanya tumbuh di sekitar pelabuhan.

rows.en: The supplier went bankrupt in March; hence the delay.
rows.id: Pemasoknya bangkrut pada bulan Maret; itulah sebabnya ada keterlambatan.

id.note: hence + kata benda, tanpa kata kerja

rows.en: The ministry launched a scheme whereby graduates repay their loans through their salaries.
rows.id: Kementerian meluncurkan skema yang memungkinkan lulusan melunasi pinjamannya lewat gaji.

id.note: kata benda + whereby + subjek + kata kerja

blocks.text:
Two common mistakes:
- `The plan was effective, albeit it was expensive.` ✗ → *The plan was effective, albeit expensive.* (or *…, although it was expensive.*)
- `Notwithstanding of the costs, we continued.` ✗ → *Notwithstanding the costs, we continued.* (*of* belongs to *in spite of*, not to *notwithstanding* or *despite*.)

Style: these words sound bookish in speech. In a meeting, *although it was expensive* and *despite the costs* sound more natural.

id.text:
Dua kesalahan umum:
- `The plan was effective, albeit it was expensive.` ✗ → *The plan was effective, albeit expensive.* (atau *…, although it was expensive.*)
- `Notwithstanding of the costs, we continued.` ✗ → *Notwithstanding the costs, we continued.* (*of* milik *in spite of*, bukan *notwithstanding* atau *despite*.)

Gaya: kata-kata ini terdengar kaku kalau diucapkan. Di rapat, *although it was expensive* dan *despite the costs* terdengar lebih wajar.

options: The results were positive, albeit they were limited.
The results were positive, albeit limited.
Albeit limited, but the results were positive.
blocks.explain: **albeit** + a short phrase (here the adjective *limited*), in the middle of the sentence. The first sentence puts a clause (*they were limited*) after albeit. The third starts with albeit and adds *but*: two linkers.

id.explain: **albeit** + frasa pendek (di sini kata sifat *limited*), di tengah kalimat. Kalimat pertama menaruh klausa (*they were limited*) setelah albeit. Kalimat ketiga dimulai dengan albeit dan menambah *but*: dua kata penghubung.

id.title: Kata penghubung formal dan tata bahasanya

blocks.text:
A long text keeps pointing back to things it has already said. Make sure the reader knows exactly **what** you point to.
- **the former** (*yang pertama / yang disebut duluan*) and **the latter** (*yang kedua / yang disebut terakhir*): only when there are exactly **two** things. With three or more, say *the first*, *the last* or name it again. They also work before a noun: *the latter option*.
- **this / these + a summary noun** (a noun that sums up the idea before it): *this approach, this trend, this decision, these findings*. It's clearer than a bare *this*.
- **such a + one thing**, **such + plural or uncountable** (*seperti itu*): *such a view, such a policy, such measures, such information*. Not `such a measures` ✗.
- **Avoid a vague this or it.** If it could point to two things, the reader has to guess: *The ministry cut the research budget and raised fees. This angered students.* Which one? → *This fee rise angered students.* The same with people: *Pak Hasan told Budi that he would lead the project.* Who will lead it? Use the name.

id.text:
Teks panjang terus merujuk balik ke hal yang sudah dikatakan. Pastikan pembaca tahu persis **apa** yang kamu rujuk.
- **the former** (*yang pertama / yang disebut duluan*) dan **the latter** (*yang kedua / yang disebut terakhir*): hanya kalau ada tepat **dua** hal. Kalau tiga atau lebih, pakai *the first*, *the last* atau sebut namanya lagi. Keduanya juga bisa dipakai sebelum kata benda: *the latter option*.
- **this / these + kata benda perangkum** (summary noun: kata benda yang merangkum ide sebelumnya): *this approach, this trend, this decision, these findings*. Lebih jelas daripada *this* saja.
- **such a + satu hal**, **such + jamak atau tak terhitung** (*seperti itu*): *such a view, such a policy, such measures, such information*. Bukan `such a measures` ✗.
- **Hindari this atau it yang kabur.** Kalau bisa merujuk ke dua hal, pembaca harus menebak: *The ministry cut the research budget and raised fees. This angered students.* Yang mana? → *This fee rise angered students.* Sama juga dengan orang: *Pak Hasan told Budi that he would lead the project.* Siapa yang akan memimpin? Sebut namanya.

rows.id: Staf bisa naik MRT atau mobil. Yang pertama (MRT) lebih cepat saat jam sibuk.

rows.en: Some schools have banned phones in class. This approach has improved concentration.
rows.id: Beberapa sekolah melarang ponsel di kelas. Cara ini meningkatkan konsentrasi.

rows.en: Online shopping keeps growing. This trend has hit small shops hard.

rows.en: These findings suggest that the programme should continue.
rows.id: Temuan-temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa programnya sebaiknya dilanjutkan.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: **hal ini / hal tersebut** appears everywhere in Indonesian formal writing, and it often becomes `this matter` or `the said matter` ✗ in English. Name the thing instead: *this problem, this delay, this policy*. And *tersebut* after a noun (*program tersebut*) is simply *this programme* or *the programme*, not `the mentioned programme` ✗. (British *programme*, American *program*.)

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: **hal ini / hal tersebut** muncul di mana-mana dalam tulisan formal bahasa Indonesia, dan sering jadi `this matter` atau `the said matter` ✗ dalam bahasa Inggris. Sebut saja bendanya: *this problem, this delay, this policy*. Dan *tersebut* setelah kata benda (*program tersebut*) cukup *this programme* atau *the programme*, bukan `the mentioned programme` ✗. (British *programme*, Amerika *program*.)

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani teaches at two universities: UI in Depok and ITB in Bandung. She spends more time at ___, as she lives in Depok.
blocks.explain: UI in Depok is mentioned first, so it is **the former**. *the latter* would be ITB in Bandung. A bare *this* doesn't say which of the two universities you mean.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani teaches at two universities: UI in Depok and ITB in Bandung. She spends more time at ___, as she lives in Depok.
id.explain: UI di Depok disebut lebih dulu, jadi itu **the former**. *the latter* adalah ITB di Bandung. *this* saja tidak menjelaskan universitas mana dari keduanya yang kamu maksud.

material.title: Signposts: the map of a long text

blocks.text:
In a long report or essay, **signposts** tell the reader where they are. They have four jobs:
- **moving to the next topic**: *Turning now to + noun, …* (a fixed phrase to remember) / *Having considered X, we now turn to Y.*
- **pointing back**: *As outlined above, …* / *As mentioned earlier, …* / *As discussed in Section 2, …*
- **pointing forward**: *As will be discussed below, …* / *This will be explained in Section 4.*
- **finding the thread again or closing**: *To return to the main point, …* / *In summary, …*

In writing, **above** = earlier in the text and **below** = later. In a presentation, say *as I mentioned earlier* and *as we'll see later*. Put signposts at the start of a paragraph or section, not in every sentence.

id.text:
Di laporan atau esai panjang, **penunjuk arah** (signpost) memberi tahu pembaca di mana mereka berada. Ada empat tugasnya:
- **pindah ke topik berikutnya**: *Turning now to + kata benda, …* (frasa tetap yang dihafal saja) / *Having considered X, we now turn to Y.*
- **merujuk ke belakang**: *As outlined above, …* / *As mentioned earlier, …* / *As discussed in Section 2, …*
- **merujuk ke depan**: *As will be discussed below, …* / *This will be explained in Section 4.*
- **kembali ke inti atau menutup**: *To return to the main point, …* / *In summary, …*

Dalam tulisan, **above** = sebelumnya di teks dan **below** = nanti. Dalam presentasi, katakan *as I mentioned earlier* dan *as we'll see later*. Taruh penunjuk arah di awal paragraf atau bagian, bukan di setiap kalimat.

rows.en: This report looks at a four-day week trial at a startup in Bandung.
rows.id: Laporan ini membahas uji coba empat hari kerja seminggu di sebuah startup di Bandung.

id.note: pendahuluan: apa yang dilakukan laporan ini

rows.en: As outlined above, 40 staff took part for six months.
rows.id: Seperti diuraikan di atas, 40 staf ikut serta selama enam bulan.

rows.en: Turning now to the costs, the figures are more mixed.
rows.id: Beralih sekarang ke biayanya, angkanya lebih beragam.

rows.en: To return to the main point, output did not fall.
rows.id: Kembali ke poin utama, hasil kerja tidak turun.

rows.en: In summary, the trial was a success, albeit a short one.
rows.id: Singkatnya, uji cobanya berhasil, meskipun singkat.

blocks.text:
Two traps:
- After *Having considered …*, the next words must be the people who considered: *Having considered the benefits, **we** now turn to the risks.* Not `Having considered the benefits, the risks will now be discussed` ✗ (the risks didn't consider anything).
- Indonesian *seperti yang telah disebutkan di atas* → *as mentioned above*, not `as above mentioned` ✗.

id.text:
Dua jebakan:
- Setelah *Having considered …*, kata berikutnya harus orang yang membahas: *Having considered the benefits, **we** now turn to the risks.* Bukan `Having considered the benefits, the risks will now be discussed` ✗ (risikonya tidak membahas apa-apa).
- *Seperti yang telah disebutkan di atas* → *as mentioned above*, bukan `as above mentioned` ✗.

options: Having considered the benefits, the risks will now be discussed.
Having considered the benefits, we now turn to the risks.
blocks.explain: The words after *Having considered …* must be the people who did the considering: **we**. In the first sentence, the grammar says the risks considered the benefits, which makes no sense.

id.explain: Kata setelah *Having considered …* harus orang yang membahas: **we**. Di kalimat pertama, tata bahasanya mengatakan risikonya yang membahas manfaatnya, dan itu tidak masuk akal.

flashcards.back: albeit: effective, albeit expensive (not albeit + subject + verb)

id.intro: Di B2 kamu sudah menghubungkan ide dengan **although**, **despite**, **whereas** dan **Nevertheless,**. Di C1 teksmu makin panjang, dan teks itu harus menyambung. Kamu akan menambah kata penghubung formal (**albeit**, **notwithstanding**, **insofar as**, **hence**, **whereby**, **in that**), merujuk balik dengan jelas memakai **the former / the latter** dan **this approach**, dan memandu pembaca melewati laporan panjang dengan penunjuk arah seperti **Turning now to …** dan **As outlined above, …**.

assessment.coh-1: Tulis albeit, notwithstanding atau insofar as. Dari laporan tentang proyek daur ulang di Surabaya: The pilot scheme was a success, ___ a modest one: only 40 households took part.
assessment.coh-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Notwithstanding of the protests, the city council approved the new toll road.
assessment.coh-3: Tulis kata yang hilang (dalam bahasa Inggris). Dari artikel berita: The new law is unusual ___ that it lets workers choose two of their own public holidays.
assessment.coh-4: Tulis dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris (bukan nama kota). Dimas was offered two scholarships: one to study in Melbourne and one to study in Leiden. He accepted ___ because his partner already works in Leiden.
assessment.coh-5: Tulis view, trend atau approach. Dari laporan perusahaan: Some managers believe that staff who work from home are lazy. However, such a ___ is not supported by the data from our survey.
assessment.coh-6: Tulis kata yang hilang (dalam bahasa Inggris). Laporan tentang uji coba empat hari kerja seminggu pindah dari produktivitas ke bagian baru: '___ now to staff opinions, most employees wanted the trial to continue.'
assessment.coh-7: Tulis kata yang hilang (dalam bahasa Inggris). Survei sudah dijelaskan di Bagian 2 sebuah laporan, dan Bagian 4 dimulai dengan: 'As outlined ___, the survey covered 300 small businesses in Yogyakarta.'
